paraphrase: The Great Perfection is distinguished from the simultaneous approach: it does not rely on the effort of fixing on non-conceptuality but on the primordially present great self-arising wisdom in which there is nothing to cultivate or reject — so Atiyoga is placed highest.

paraphrase: Nupchen presents the gradual approach (rim gyis pa) taught by Kamalaśīla — calm and analytical insight cultivated step by step — as authentic but the lowest of the four approaches he compares.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge (not read in a local text in this phase). Section-level locator; chapter numbers not recorded.

paraphrase: The simultaneous approach (cig car ba) of the Chan master Moheyan — entering non-conceptuality directly without gradual steps — is presented with respect as higher than the gradual, yet below Mahāyoga and the Great Perfection.
